subject: maths
question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: A square is a special case of neither a rectangle nor a rhombus.
A square is a special case of a rhombus only.
A square is a special case of both a rectangle and a rhombus
A square is a special case of a rectangle only

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A rectangle requires all its internal angles to be exactly 90°.

A rhombus requires all its four sides to be equal in length.

A square is a shape that has all 90° angles AND all equal sides.

Since it meets all the defining conditions of both shapes, it inherently belongs to both families.

**∴ The correct answer is both a rectangle and a rhombus.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Statements comparing a square to a rectangle and a rhombus.

**Properties Used:**

Definitions of Quadrilaterals (Rectangle, Rhombus, and Square)

**Calculations:**

⇒ By definition, a rectangle is a quadrilateral where all internal angles measure exactly 90°.

⇒ A rhombus is defined as a quadrilateral where all four sides are of equal length.

⇒ A square is constructed as a quadrilateral where all four sides are equal AND all four internal angles measure exactly 90°.

⇒ Since a square exhibits opposite sides being equal and all angles as 90°, it completely satisfies the properties of a rectangle.

⇒ Since a square has all four sides equal, it also satisfies the core geometric property of a rhombus.

⇒ Thus, a square inherently functions as a special specialized subset of both figures simultaneously.

**∴ The correct answer is both a rectangle and a rhombus.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Parallelogram Hierarchy

A parallelogram is a quadrilateral with opposite sides parallel and equal. Rectangles, rhombuses, and squares are all categorized as special types of parallelograms.

Trapezium

A trapezium (or trapezoid) is a quadrilateral that possesses exactly one pair of opposite parallel sides, setting it apart from the dual-parallel structure of parallelograms.

Diagonals Property

The diagonals of a rectangle are always equal in length. The diagonals of a rhombus always bisect each other at precisely 90°. A square inherits both rules simultaneously.
